name: Depaving
reason: The deliberate removal of sealed surface to expose soil. Called an enabling intervention by the source, but unlike the soil operations of section 19 the intervention is itself the change of surface, and the permeable plaza was kept on the same de-sealing logic.
cooling_mechanism: reduced heat storage from de-sealing + evapotranspiration once planted

name: Sandarium
reason: Bare exposed sand. No cited evidence class in the library describes it and there is no envelope to inherit; a biodiversity element, not a cooling intervention.
cooling_mechanism: None directly. Indirect biodiversity benefits only.

name: Habitat Gravel Patch
reason: Bare mineral surface, which stores heat rather than losing it. Same reasoning as the sandarium.

name: Live Fascines
reason: A construction technique for soft bank protection, which is the system the living shoreline already names. Defined a second time in the source as 11B.2.
cooling_mechanism: increased evapotranspiration; riparian shading after establishment

name: Live Stakes
reason: Point reinforcement by dormant cuttings: a planting method within the bank system, not a system. Defined a second time as 11B.3.

name: Brush Mattress
reason: Surface treatment of an eroding bank whose temporary structural components degrade over time; the finished thing is a vegetated bank.

name: Brush Layering
reason: Alternating branch and soil layers within a reconstructed bank. Defined a second time as 11B.1.

name: Live Cribwall
reason: A timber crib that becomes a living retaining structure; the timber eventually decomposes and the vegetated bank remains.

name: Vegetated Geogrid
reason: Reinforcement material within a vegetated bank build-up. Defined a second time as 11B.6.

name: Vegetated Coir Roll (Coir Log)
reason: Biodegradable toe protection of limited lifespan: a material within the bank system.

name: Willow Spiling
reason: A traditional weaving technique producing the same vegetated bank.

name: Vegetated Riprap
reason: Rock armour with planting between; the source's own caveat is that it is less natural than purely vegetated systems.

name: Rootwad Revetment
reason: Anchored dead tree root masses in the channel. It carries no vegetation of its own, so there is no vegetated envelope to inherit; the shade it claims belongs to bank planting it does not contain.

name: Engineered Log Jam
reason: Anchored large woody material for channel morphology and fish habitat. Requires hydraulic modelling, and belongs to river engineering rather than the urban public realm.

name: Reed Bed Stabilisation
reason: Emergent vegetation establishing on saturated margins: the vegetated state of the bank system rather than a separate one.

name: Riparian Brush Planting
reason: Dense native shrub planting on a bank: the planting layer of the same system.

name: Live Brush Layering
reason: A deep-reinforcement technique within a reconstructed slope; the finished thing is a vegetated slope. Defined a second time as 11.4.

name: Live Fascines
reason: Contour bundles intercepting runoff: a technique. Defined a second time as 11.1.

name: Live Stakes
reason: Point reinforcement with limited structural capacity during establishment. Defined a second time as 11.2.

name: Vegetated Geocells
reason: Cellular confinement filled and vegetated: a manufactured material within a vegetated slope.

name: Vegetated Geomats
reason: An erosion-control mat protecting soil while vegetation becomes established; the mat is scaffolding for the entry it merges into.

name: Vegetated Geogrids
reason: Reinforcement material. Defined a second time as 11.6.

name: Vegetated Rock Gabions
reason: The source concedes it qualifies only where vegetation forms an integral component of the system: the vegetation is the NbS and the gabion is the structure.

name: Vegetated Reinforced Earth
reason: Mechanically stabilised earth supporting vegetated cover; engineering intensive, same vegetated outcome.

name: Shrub Stabilisation
reason: Dense shrub planting on a slope: the planting layer of the kept entry.

name: Deep-rooted Native Planting
reason: Native trees and shrubs for root reinforcement, which is what the kept entry's native vegetation means.

name: Grass Reinforcement
reason: Fibrous-rooted grass cover; the source itself flags limited habitat and low biodiversity where monocultures are used.

name: Hydroseeding
reason: Disqualified by its own classification note: a supporting revegetation technique rather than a high-value Nature-based Solution unless diverse native species are deliberately incorporated, with relatively low ecological value stated twice.

name: Coconut Fibre Blanket
reason: A temporary natural-fibre blanket: a material, and one of three near-identical ones.

name: Jute Erosion Mat
reason: The same function and lifespan as the coconut-fibre blanket in a different fibre.

name: Biodegradable Erosion-Control Blanket
reason: The generic superset of the coconut-fibre and jute variants; merging material variants into one entry is what the catalogue already does for cable and trellis facades.

name: Vegetated Terracing
reason: Stepped terraces that change the landform rather than merely its cover: a distinct construction with its own water-retention behaviour, and the only slope entry that alters gradient rather than reinforcing it.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from terraced planting + water retained on the slope

name: Natural Slope Restoration
reason: The canonical vegetated slope: native vegetation and soil rehabilitation instead of conventional hard engineering. The catalogue had no slope entry of any kind, and embankments, cuttings and landslide scars are ordinary urban conditions.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from re-established native slope vegetation

name: Horizontal Subsurface Flow Constructed Wetland
reason: Shipped as Subsurface-flow treatment wetland. The flow is beneath a gravel bed, so there is no exposed water surface: inheriting the constructed-wetland class on the strength of the word wetland would attribute evaporative cooling to water that is under stone.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from emergent planting over a gravel bed; no exposed water surface

name: Vertical Flow Treatment Wetland
reason: A hydraulic configuration of the same subsurface system; greater oxygen transfer is a treatment property, not a thermal one.

name: Hybrid Constructed Wetland
reason: By its own definition a combination of the horizontal and vertical flow entries.

name: Floating Treatment Wetland
reason: The catalogue already carries the floating planted platform; the influent is an attribute.

name: Biofiltration Basin
reason: Engineered media, vegetation, storage and underdrainage: the bioretention entry described again.

name: Living Machine
reason: A trademarked proprietary treatment train rather than a typology, partly indoor, and requiring specialist operation.

name: Planted Sand Filter
reason: Subsurface filtration through planted sand media: the same no-open-water system in a different medium.

name: Reed Bed Treatment System
reason: Self-declared to be on a different classification axis: a plant community typology, whereas the other wetland categories describe hydraulic treatment configurations. The canonical reed bed is subsurface.

name: Ecological Wastewater Treatment Wetland
reason: Physically the catalogue's constructed wetland; what differs is pollutant load, an attribute the tool does not score.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration; vegetation; open water where present

name: Constructed Sewage Wetland
reason: Optimised for sewage treatment at larger scales: influent and scale, not form.

name: Waste Stabilisation Pond
reason: Municipal sanitation works of 1,000-100,000 square metres with potential odour and mosquito management. Not an intervention offered for an urban site.

name: Anaerobic Treatment Wetland
reason: Functions as a first-stage treatment system rather than a complete process, at municipal or industrial scale, with odour.

name: Facultative Treatment Lagoon
reason: A municipal treatment lagoon with algal and mosquito management; same reasoning as the waste stabilisation pond.

name: Polishing Wetland
reason: Its own text states it is not suitable as a standalone wastewater treatment system, being a stage within a treatment train. Where landscape-integrated it is a constructed wetland.

name: Recycled Water Irrigation Network
reason: A pipe network that distributes already treated water rather than treating it. This is the irrigation the methodology already models as sustaining an entry within its envelope and never as raising it.

name: Landscape Water Reuse System
reason: Self-declared an integrated landscape management system: a management objective over kept entries.
cooling_mechanism: sustained evapotranspiration; irrigated vegetation; increased soil moisture

name: Rainwater Harvesting Landscape
reason: A water-supply strategy realised through rain gardens, bioswales and storage: a package of kept entries, the ruling that dropped the urban sponge landscape.
cooling_mechanism: sustained irrigation; increased evapotranspiration; improved soil moisture

name: Stormwater Harvesting Landscape
reason: The same as rainwater harvesting with urban runoff as the source; the difference is the source, not the form.

name: Managed Aquifer Recharge Landscape
reason: Stores water below ground and lists minimal evaporation losses as an advantage: the cooling mechanism is the one it is designed to suppress.
cooling_mechanism: increased soil moisture; vegetation supported through groundwater

name: Seasonal Water Storage Landscape
reason: Temporal redistribution of water: a water-management objective at district-to-regional scale.
cooling_mechanism: supports irrigation; sustains evapotranspiration during drought

name: Water Plaza with Reuse
reason: Cross-references the water square itself and differs only by planned water reuse, a hydraulic setting.
cooling_mechanism: evaporation; irrigated vegetation; increased soil moisture

name: Irrigation Wetland
reason: Its own text: functions primarily as a water distribution and storage landscape. Physically a constructed wetland.

name: Nutrient Recovery Wetland
reason: The objective is resource recovery, and the source states the form is unchanged.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration; vegetation; open water where present

name: Biomass Harvest Wetland
reason: Differentiated only by a harvesting regime: a management practice, not a form.

name: Productive Treatment Wetland
reason: Productive outputs are deliberately incorporated, but food crops are generally inappropriate, so it is not a productive-landscape entry either.

name: Agro-wetland
reason: District to regional, peri-urban, 1,000-100,000 square metres, with agricultural suitability dependent on regulatory standards: a peri-urban agricultural land use.

name: Constructed Reed Harvest System
reason: Distinguished from the reed bed treatment system by a maintenance regime alone, on the source's own account.

name: Living Shoreline
reason: The catalogue already ships this entry under this name, kept with the note that it covers coastal and freshwater shores alike.

name: Oyster Reef Restoration
reason: A submerged marine ecosystem: no pedestrian-level effect and no envelope to inherit.

name: Seagrass Restoration
reason: Fully submerged meadows in shallow coastal water.

name: Mangrove Restoration
reason: Woody vegetation restored on a tidal margin, cooling by shade and evapotranspiration. It inherits the cited class for water-margin woodland, and is the one envelope in this curation applied outside the biome its evidence measured; a per-entry override restricts it to the tropical zones on the source's own words.
cooling_mechanism: canopy shade over the intertidal margin + evapotranspiration

name: Saltmarsh Restoration
reason: Tidal saltmarsh is the coastal wetland under another name, with an identical sole cooling mechanism and overlapping applications.

name: Dune Restoration
reason: Native dune vegetation and sand management: a distinct coastal landform system. Deliberately not merged into the coastal park, which is a park and reports established-park values a restored dune does not earn.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from dune vegetation + reduced bare-sand surface heating

name: Coastal Wetland Restoration
reason: Tidal and brackish wetland: emergent vegetation standing in shallow water, not open water. The large-water-body class was considered and rejected for the reason the two water archetypes are kept apart at all.

name: Beach Nourishment with Dune Vegetation
reason: The vegetative half is dune restoration; the other half is sediment import, an engineering operation the tool does not score.

name: Coastal Bioengineering
reason: Living vegetation and natural materials stabilising coastal slopes, bluffs and shorelines: the definition of the entry it merges into.

name: Hybrid Living Breakwater
reason: An engineered offshore breakwater with ecological components: grey infrastructure in the water column.

name: Kelp Forest Restoration
reason: Submerged macroalgae, restricted to suitable cold and temperate marine environments.

name: Ground-rooted Climber System
reason: Restates the indirect ground-rooted facade, including its cable and trellis support options, which is why the cable and mesh variants merged into it already.
cooling_mechanism: shade; evapotranspiration; reduced facade heat gain

name: Wall-mounted Living Wall
reason: Plants installed within engineered panels fixed to the facade is the modular living wall's definition.

name: Cable Trellis System
reason: The cable facade, already merged into the indirect ground-rooted facade once.

name: Modular Living Wall
reason: The catalogue entry of the same name, and a near-duplicate of the wall-mounted living wall within its own chapter.

name: Planter-box Facade
reason: Rooting in planters at multiple levels is the planter-rooted facade.

name: Green Loggia
reason: A recessed planted outdoor room with restricted air movement and high radiant load from the surrounding fabric: the enclosed-courtyard geometry at building scale. No counterpart in the catalogue, and distinguished by the source from both balcony and terrace.
cooling_mechanism: shade and evapotranspiration within a recessed, poorly ventilated volume

name: Green Atrium
reason: Indoor: a planted internal or semi-enclosed atrium improving indoor environmental quality, functioning as an interior climate landscape. The same entry was already dropped once, as 9.31, for the same reason.

name: Indoor Biophilic System
reason: Indoor, and self-limiting: limited cooling effect, primarily designed for interior environments rather than external building envelopes.

name: Vertical Forest Building
reason: A building carrying substantial tree and shrub planting across its balconies and terraces: a distinct built form with no catalogue counterpart. It inherits the facade class and not dense canopy, because the vegetated-balcony figures of kumar2024 were deliberately not adopted so that balconies would not outscore measured street trees.
cooling_mechanism: facade shading and evapotranspiration from balcony-borne trees and shrubs

name: Sky Garden
reason: Integrated at intermediate levels within the building rather than on its roof: a position, not a form, the same reasoning under which the green verge merged into the green median.

name: Roof Forest
reason: The catalogue entry restated: multiple trees and layered vegetation on a roof, distinguished from an intensive roof in the same words.

name: Bee Hotel
reason: Artificial nesting cavities. No cooling mechanism is stated and there is no envelope to inherit.

name: Bat Box
reason: An artificial roost fixed to a building or tree, with no thermal function.

name: Bird Nesting Wall
reason: Nesting cavities integrated into masonry: a building component, not vegetation.

name: Swift Brick
reason: A single brick with a cavity.

name: Hedgehog Highway
reason: A gap in a fence: the intervention is an absence of material, and it is self-declared to be about landscape connectivity rather than habitat creation.

name: Deadwood Habitat Pile
reason: Retained dead wood for decomposers; also duplicated in the source as 20.5.

name: Log Pile Habitat
reason: Stacked logs, given as a stub entry with no scale, advantages or limitations.

name: Stone Pile Habitat
reason: The only entry in the section to state a cooling mechanism, and it states none. It is also thermally counter-directional by design: warm crevices requiring sun exposure.

name: Hibernaculum
reason: A frost-free overwintering refuge: an insulating device, not a summer cooling one.

name: Amphibian Shelter
reason: A refuge structure; the only cool in the entry is the microhabitat for the animal inside it.

name: Reptile Basking Habitat
reason: Exposed sun-heated rock for thermoregulation: a warming feature, and a combination of the log and stone piles.

name: Insect Hotel
reason: The multi-species superset of the bee hotel; same reasoning.

name: Sandarium (previously defined)
reason: A duplicate of A17 pointing at an unresolved placeholder. A17 is dropped, so this is dropped on the same grounds.

name: Habitat Gravel Patch (previously defined)
reason: A duplicate of A18, likewise.

name: Soil Decompaction
reason: Cooling stated as mediated through healthier vegetation rather than direct. An enabling soil operation, listed by the source as a component of depaving.
cooling_mechanism: increased infiltration; improved soil moisture; enhanced evapotranspiration through healthier vegetation

name: Soil Regeneration
reason: Self-declared umbrella: integrates multiple restoration techniques rather than a single intervention, with supporting all subsequent NbS as its stated advantage.
cooling_mechanism: improved water retention; increased vegetation performance

name: Soil Remediation
reason: The parent category of phytoremediation and mycoremediation, defined by the contaminant rather than by a form.

name: Phytoremediation
reason: The only entry in the section whose mechanism is the planting: it uses living vegetation as the primary remediation mechanism. It also answers a planning case the catalogue could not, the contaminated site.

name: Mycoremediation
reason: Indirect, and an emerging practice with site-specific performance by its own limitations.

name: Biochar Incorporation
reason: A soil amendment whose cooling runs through enhanced vegetation performance.
cooling_mechanism: improved soil moisture; enhanced vegetation performance

name: Compost Amendment
reason: A soil amendment whose cooling runs through improved vegetation growth.
cooling_mechanism: increased soil moisture; improved vegetation growth

name: Topsoil Restoration
reason: Reconstruction of a soil horizon so that vegetation can later be planted.

name: Subsoil Rehabilitation
reason: The lower half of topsoil restoration; the stated mechanisms are hydrological and root, not thermal.

name: Structural Soil
reason: The catalogue entry restated. Its own text calls it one of the most important enabling technologies, and it is defined a second time in the source as 15.4.10, in a family whose note says they are not Nature-based Solutions in themselves.
cooling_mechanism: enhanced tree growth; increased evapotranspiration; increased infiltration

name: Living Soil
reason: A soil condition maintained by management, self-flagged as difficult to quantify and requiring adaptive management.
cooling_mechanism: improved vegetation performance; increased water retention

name: Microbial Inoculation
reason: Indirect through healthier vegetation, by its own statement.

name: Reduced Mowing
reason: Management changes rather than physical intervention, in the source's own words. Its outcome, a meadow, is the pocket meadow already in the catalogue.
cooling_mechanism: increased evapotranspiration; greater vegetation cover; reduced surface temperatures

name: Seasonal Mowing
reason: The same practice parameterised by timing rather than frequency.

name: Adaptive Irrigation
reason: An irrigation schedule. The methodology already treats irrigation as sustaining an entry within its envelope and never as raising it, so scoring it as an intervention would double-count.

name: Ecological Pruning
reason: A maintenance mode preserving an existing asset rather than adding one.
cooling_mechanism: maintains effective canopy cover; supports long-term shading

name: Deadwood Retention
reason: An act of non-removal; duplicated in the source as 18.6.

name: Natural Succession Management
reason: A management strategy of minimal intervention. Where it produces a real outcome on a real site, that outcome is brownfield ecological succession, which is kept.

name: Seasonal Flooding Management
reason: The planned acceptance and management of temporary flooding; the physical intervention it presupposes is the floodable or stormwater park already catalogued.
cooling_mechanism: increased soil moisture; surface water evaporation

name: Rotational Grazing
reason: A grazing regime, suitable only for larger landscapes.

name: Adaptive Planting
reason: The ongoing adjustment of species composition: planting evolves over time rather than remaining fixed after construction.
cooling_mechanism: improved vegetation performance; sustained canopy cover; increased evapotranspiration

name: Climate-resilient Maintenance
reason: An umbrella over the other management entries by its own definition, applying to all Nature-based Solutions; its limitations are institutional rather than physical.
cooling_mechanism: sustained vegetation health; long-term ecosystem performance

name: Grassland Restoration
reason: Native grass and herbaceous re-establishment: the same vegetation structure and cooling behaviour as the catalogue's meadow entry. Extent is a parameter, not a typology.

name: Meadow Restoration
reason: The catalogue's meadow entry under another name, distinguished from grassland restoration only by flowering herbaceous diversity, a species-selection objective.

name: Heathland Restoration
reason: Limited geographical suitability, cooling stated as vegetation cover alone, and no urban setting among its applications.

name: Peatland Restoration
reason: Limited geographical occurrence, landscape to regional in scale, with stated advantages that are global carbon rather than local cooling.

name: Shrubland Restoration
reason: The same vegetation structure and cooling behaviour as the shrub-dominated planting bed; restoration versus creation is a delivery mode the catalogue distinguishes only where an availability gate turns on it, as it does for woodland.

name: Riparian Habitat Restoration
reason: The tool's own riparian restoration, restated. River restoration is the target rather than the riparian buffer because this entry recovers natural hydrology as well as bank vegetation, where the buffer is explicitly a discrete vegetated strip.

name: Urban Ecological Restoration
reason: Neighbourhood to city in scale and subsuming the other restoration entries: a programme over kept entries, the ruling that dropped the ecological network.

name: Brownfield Ecological Succession
reason: Managed natural colonisation of a former industrial site, where the intervention is largely the decision not to intervene. There is no catalogue equivalent, the naturalistic park being a park, and the archetype's genuine zero floor suits a site in its first seasons.
cooling_mechanism: evapotranspiration from spontaneous pioneer vegetation as cover establishes

name: Native Habitat Restoration
reason: A self-declared catch-all that targets no specific ecosystem type: a composition attribute, like native woodland before it.

name: Wildlife Overpass (Eco-bridge)
reason: Regional transport infrastructure; the vegetation it carries is not sited where people stand.

name: Wildlife Underpass
reason: A tunnel beneath a road.

name: Amphibian Tunnel
reason: A species-specific narrowing of the wildlife underpass.

name: Fish Passage
reason: A hydraulic structure requiring river engineering.

name: Bat Flyway
reason: Its physical substance is tree lines and hedgerows, which are the corridor entries already kept.

name: Arboreal Rope Bridge
reason: A rope between two existing canopies.

name: Infiltration Trench
reason: A buried stone-filled trench whose stated cooling belongs to surrounding vegetation it does not contain.
cooling_mechanism: increased soil moisture; enhanced evapotranspiration through surrounding vegetation

name: Infiltration Gallery
reason: A larger infiltration trench, listing hidden infrastructure as an advantage.
cooling_mechanism: increased groundwater recharge; enhanced vegetation performance

name: Tree Trench
reason: The catalogue entry restated verbatim, down to the same contrast with individual tree pits.

name: Structural Stormwater Trench
reason: Self-described drainage infrastructure beneath pavement.
cooling_mechanism: increased soil moisture; enhanced vegetation performance

name: Underground Soil Cell System
reason: The catalogue entry restated; it names proprietary products, and its own text calls it an underground support system.

name: Modular Stormwater Crate System
reason: Manufactured plastic crates, with cooling stated as indirect.
cooling_mechanism: Indirect through water availability for vegetation.

name: Tree Irrigation Reservoir
reason: A buried reservoir; the cooling listed is the tree's.

name: Root Barrier System
reason: Indirect by its own statement, with infrastructure protection as its stated ecosystem service.

name: Root Path System
reason: A buried conduit, indirect by its own statement.

name: Stormwater Distribution Chamber
reason: A hydraulic control node whose stated service is improved NbS performance: it services other entries rather than being one.
